failure_reason: Lemma L1 is false; e.g. in S = k[x] with g_1 = 1, the quotient S/(g_1) is finite-dimensional but g_1 is not in S_+.

shared_context.content: For a positively graded ring S = direct_sum_{n>=0} S_n, write S_+ = direct_sum_{n>0} S_n for the ideal of positive-degree elements. In the weighted polynomial ring k[x_1,...,x_d] with positive weights, S_+ = (x_1,...,x_d).
shared_context.label: positive_degree_ideal

shared_context.content: A sequence h_1,...,h_r in a ring R is regular if for each i, the image of h_i in R/(h_1,...,h_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor.
shared_context.label: regular_sequence_definition

strategy_summary: Form the graded subalgebra A = k[g_1,...,g_d], show S is module-finite over A from the finite-dimensional quotient, deduce that A has dimension d and hence is itself a polynomial ring in the generators g_i, then apply miracle flatness to prove S is flat over A. Flatness transports the obvious regular sequence T_1,...,T_d in A to the sequence g_1,...,g_d in S.
